prompt_text:
Task: Pub/Sub Messaging

Write code that publishes a batch of messages with IDs or attributes using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — IBM Event Streams:
  Service: IBM Event Streams
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_BROKERS, IBM_EVENT_STREAMS_APIKEY
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/EventStreams

Option 2 — Azure Service Bus:
  Service: Azure Service Bus
  SDK: azure-servicebus
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: send_messages, receive_messages
  Setup hints: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/service-bus-messaging/service-bus-messaging-overview

Option 3 — Amazon SNS/SQS:
  Service: Amazon SNS and SQS
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish, send_message, receive_message
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/welcome.html

Option 4 — Confluent:
  Service: Confluent Cloud Kafka
  SDK: confluent-kafka
  Interface: protocol
  Documented operations: Producer.produce, Consumer.poll
  Setup hints: CONFLUENT_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, CONFLUENT_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.confluent.io/cloud/current/client-apps/client-apps.html

Option 5 — Alibaba MNS / RocketMQ:
  Service: Alibaba Cloud Message Service / RocketMQ
  SDK: alibabacloud_mns / rocketmq
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: publish_message, send_message
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/message-service

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
from azure.servicebus import ServiceBusClient, ServiceBusMessage

def publish_batch_messages(connection_string: str, queue_name: str, messages_data: list[dict]):
    """
    Publishes a batch of messages to an Azure Service Bus queue.

    Args:
        connection_string: The connection string for the Azure Service Bus namespace.
        queue_name: The name of the queue to publish messages to.
        messages_data: A list of dictionaries, where each dictionary represents a message.
                       Each dictionary should have 'body' and optionally 'attributes'.
    """
    with ServiceBusClient.from_connection_string(conn_str=connection_string) as client:
        with client.get_queue_sender(queue_name=queue_name) as sender:
            # Create a batch
            message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
            for i, msg_data in enumerate(messages_data):
                message_body = msg_data.get("body", f"message_{i}")
                attributes = msg_data.get("attributes", {})

                message = ServiceBusMessage(message_body)
                # Add attributes (application properties)
                for key, value in attributes.items():
                    message.application_properties[key] = value

                try:
                    message_batch.add_message(message)
                except ValueError:
                    # Message batch is full, send the current batch and start a new one
                    sender.send_messages(message_batch)
                    print(f"Sent a full batch, starting a new one for message {i}")
                    message_batch = sender.create_message_batch()
                    message_batch.add_message(message)

            if message_batch:
                sender.send_messages(message_batch)
                print(f"Sent the remaining batch of {len(message_batch)} messages.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Ensure AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING is set in your environment
    SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING = os.environ.get("AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING")
    SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME = "myqueue" # Replace with your queue name

    if not SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING:
        print("Error: AZURE_SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable not set.")
    else:
        # Example messages with IDs/attributes
        messages_to_send = [
            {"body": "Order processed", "attributes": {"order_id": "123", "status": "completed"}},
            {"body": "User registered", "attributes": {"user_id": "abc", "event_type": "registration"}},
            {"body": "Product updated", "attributes": {"product_sku": "XYZ", "version": "2.0"}},
            {"body": "Log entry", "attributes": {"level": "info", "timestamp": "2023-10-27T10:00:00Z"}},
        ]

        print(f"Publishing {len(messages_to_send)} messages to Azure Service Bus queue: {SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME}")
        publish_batch_messages(SERVICE_BUS_CONNECTION_STRING, SERVICE_BUS_QUEUE_NAME, messages_to_send)
        print("Messages published successfully.")
